title: Proportion of Bankruptcies due to Credit Card Debts
what_it_is: Proportion of Bankruptcies due to Credit Card Debts

sections.label: Bankruptcy orders and non-performing loans
sections.summary: Bankruptcy orders in the first half of 2024 were stable versus recent years and below pre-COVID-19 levels, with NPLs under 1% of individual loans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The number of bankruptcy orders in the first half of 2024 has been stable compared to the same period in the last few years and remains below pre-COVID-19 levels.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Non-performing loans (NPLs) are less than 1% of all loans to individuals extended by financial institutions as of the second quarter of 2024.

sections.label: Bankruptcy orders from business failures
sections.summary: Slightly over two-fifths of bankruptcy orders in the first half of 2024 were due to business failures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Slightly over two-fifths of bankruptcy orders were due to business failures in the first half of 2024.

sections.label: BNPL share of card payments
sections.summary: In Singapore, the BNPL sector remains relatively small, with transactions totalling about 1% of total credit and debit card payments in the first half of 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: In fact, in Singapore, the BNPL sector is still relatively small and transactions now total about 1% of total credit and debit card payments in the first half of 2023.

sections.label: Bankruptcy applications versus orders
sections.summary: While bankruptcy applications picked up in the first half of 2024, not all applications result in bankruptcy orders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: One, to reiterate the point that while bankruptcy applications have picked up in the first half of 2024, not all of these bankruptcy applications result in bankruptcy orders.

sections.label: Mortgage stress tests and repayment risks
sections.summary: MAS stress tests suggest most households can service mortgage debt even with around 10% income losses and 5.5% mortgage rates, though a small segment of highly leveraged borrowers with below median incomes may be more vulnerable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: I mentioned earlier on that bankruptcy orders have been stable despite elevated interest rates – and I know interest rates are now moderating – and also, economic uncertainties continue to persist.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: But our MAS stress tests suggest that even now, most households should still be able to service their mortgage debt, even under conservative scenarios of significant income losses of around 10% and even at elevated mortgage rates of 5.5%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: And even in the above stress test scenarios, at elevated interest rates, households would still be able to service their mortgages from financial institutions, although a very small segment, the one that Mr Derrick Goh mentioned, of highly leveraged borrowers with below median household incomes, could be more vulnerable to repayment risks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: But such borrowers also account for less than 5% of total mortgage loans by count and comprise mostly private housing loans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Looking ahead, given the expected decline in domestic interest rates, we think that it should ease debt repayment for borrowers.
